record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can technology-enabled social distancing systems collect and use sensitive data such as face or appearance information, exact locations, trajectories, travel records, contact histories, and health conditions while providing privacy-preserving and cybersecurity protections that keep individual users’ sensitive information private?

evidence.quote: Most aforementioned social distancing scenarios (see Table III for more details) call for people’s private information, to a different extent, ranging from their face/appearance to location, travel records, or health condition/data.
Given that, to enable technology-based social distancing, it is critical to develop privacy-preserving and cybersecurity solutions to ensure that users’ private data are properly used and protected.
The general principle of users’ privacy-preserving is to keep each individual user’s sensitive information private when the available data are being publicly accessed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a data-driven social-distancing monitoring system that, in order to detect proximity violations and assess infection risk among a population of users, must collect and process highly sensitive personal data of each user, including: (i) facial images and appearance features, (ii) precise geolocation coordinates, (iii) movement trajectories over time, (iv) travel records, (v) contact histories with other users, and (vi) health conditions and medical data. Suppose this data is aggregated and made available for analysis by parties such as health authorities, researchers, or service providers.

Design a framework of cryptographic, statistical, and system-level mechanisms (for example, secure multi-party computation, homomorphic encryption, differential privacy, federated learning, secure enclaves, anonymization, and access control) such that the following properties hold simultaneously:

1. Utility: the system can still accurately perform the social-distancing tasks it is intended for (e.g., detecting close contacts, identifying high-risk areas, contact tracing, exposure notification).
2. Privacy preservation: no individual user's sensitive information of any of the types (i)–(vi) above can be inferred by an adversary with publicly accessible data, beyond a quantifiable and small leakage bound.
3. Cybersecurity: the system is robust against standard adversarial attacks, including data breaches, inference attacks, re-identification attacks, and collusion among a bounded subset of participating parties.

Formally specify such a scheme, prove its correctness and security under a clearly stated threat model, and quantify the trade-off between utility loss and privacy guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad, open research direction in privacy-preserving computing for pandemic-era contact tracing and social distancing. While many partial solutions exist (e.g., DP-3T, Google/Apple Exposure Notification, differential privacy frameworks, federated learning), there is no single comprehensive scheme that simultaneously protects all listed sensitive data types with proven utility-privacy trade-offs. The problem remains an active open research area.

status_evidence.title: DP-3T Decentralized Privacy-Preserving Proximity Tracing
status_evidence.snippet: DP-3T provides decentralized proximity tracing but does not cover facial, trajectory, or health-record privacy in a unified framework.
status_evidence.claim: Existing protocols solve only sub-parts of the stated problem.

status_evidence.title: Privacy-Preserving Contact Tracing: Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys outline numerous open challenges in unifying privacy across heterogeneous sensitive data sources used for pandemic monitoring.
status_evidence.claim: Comprehensive privacy-preserving frameworks for combined sensitive-data social distancing remain open.
